summary: Iteration 2 testing: all 4 NEW features (Telegram notification-settings, POP /test-connection, POP edit live config, Map route editing) + 2 regressions (topology engine simulate-fault, malformed Bearer -> 401) PASS. Backend: 19/19 pytest at /app/backend/tests/test_popmon_iter2.py (+ iter1 test file preserved). Frontend: admin login works, Settings page shows Telegram card with all testids (notif-enabled, notif-token, notif-chatid, notif-save-btn, notif-test-btn), POP page action menu pop-actions-POP-A opens dialog with pop-edit-POP-A -> edit-sim/edit-method/test-connection-btn/pop-edit-save; Test Connection button returned test-result with 'FAILED Host not reachable (ICMP)' (as expected on private IPs), Map toolbar has map-mode-editlink and clicking a cable line reveals save-route-btn with draggable vertices, mobile viewport (390x844) hides sidebar and shows sidebar-toggle hamburger that opens drawer with full nav. State mutations restored (pop-a sim re-enabled with ether1/ether2/ether3, pop-a interfaces_down cleared, link-ab route kept as 3-point line per instructions, notifications disabled with fake token kept token_enc for has_token verification but ns.enabled=false).
critical_code_review_comments: api.py update_pop: when the client sends `interfaces: ['ether1','ether2']` for a POP that originally had 3 interfaces (ether3) the extra interface is silently removed; test exposed that this breaks topology (LINK-AD becomes UNKNOWN because POP-A no longer has ether3). This is the DESIGN of the endpoint (full replace), but there's no server-side guard preventing clients from accidentally orphaning links. Suggestion: on PUT /pops/{id}, if removing an interface used by any link, either refuse (400) or auto-mark link UNKNOWN with a reason. Documented behavior would also help.

notifications.send_test / send_message: when enabled=false it returns {ok:false, message:'Notifications disabled'} which the Settings UI will show as a failure toast — that's accurate but confusing after user clicks 'Send Test'. Consider sending a test attempt regardless of enabled flag, OR hint 'enable alerts first'.

POST /notification-settings/test uses the stored (encrypted) token via send_message; because a fake token was PUT in tests the real Telegram API will return 404 (bot not found). The current code catches this via HTTP code path and returns {ok:false, message:'Telegram HTTP 404: ...'}, which is correct non-500 behavior.
api.py update_pop: `simulation_enabled` body key maps to Mongo dot-path `simulation.enabled` via $set — works fine. Interfaces list replace preserves existing counters by name map — good.

monitor.py _collect: in LIVE mode when pop has no mikrotik_ip the first branch (`sim.enabled or not mikrotik_ip`) actually keeps it in simulation (good). But operator may expect LIVE mode without an IP to go DOWN; current code hides this. Minor.
(From iter1 and still present) Login brute-force lockout stores locked_until=now, so 429 never triggers. Not blocking iter2 scope.

Known caveat: TestPopEdit replaces pop-a interfaces and the test file explicitly restores ether1/ether2/ether3; if you add further tests that touch pop-a interfaces, restore the same 3 ifaces or LINK-AD will become UNKNOWN and the alt-path regression will fail. Map polyline click in Playwright requires using element.bounding_box() + page.mouse.click() rather than locator.click(force=True), because leaflet-interactive paths need real mouse events to fire the Leaflet click handler.
